messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Turkish, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Turkish line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
118 Sonra ateşte memnun olanları göreceksin 119 ateşte çünkü gelmeyi umuyorlar, 120 ne zaman olursa olsun kutsal halka.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑by‑Word Alignment Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|-----------------------|----------------------|------------------------|--------| | **e** | coordinating conjunction “and then” | **Sonra** | “afterwards / then” | OK | | **vederai** | 2nd sg. future “you will see” | **göreceksin** | “you will see” | OK | | **color** | demonstrative plural “those (people)” | **olanları** | “those (who …)” | OK | | **che** (rel. pron.) | introduces relative clause “who” | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** (implicit in “memnun olanları”) | | **son** | copular verb “are” | **memnun** | “contented” (adjective) | **UNNECESSARY** (copula dropped) | | **contenti** | adjective “contented, satisfied” | **memnun** | “contented” | OK | | **nel** | preposition “in the” | **ateşte** | “in the fire” | OK | | **foco** | noun “fire” | **ateşte** | “in the fire” | OK | | **perché** | causal conjunction “because” | **çünkü** | “because” | OK | | **speran** | 3rd pl. present “they hope” | **umuyorlar** | “they hope” | OK | | **di** | infinitive marker “to” (Italian) | **gelmeyi** | “to come” (gerund) | OK | | **venire** | infinitive “to come” | **gelmeyi** | “to come” | OK | | **quando** | temporal adverb “whenever” | **ne** | “when” (as part of “ne zaman”) | OK | | **che** (temporal particle) | reinforces “quando” | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | **sia** | subjunctive “may be” | **olursa** | “if/should be” | OK | | **a** | preposition “to” | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** (direction expressed by case) | | **le** | definite article (fem. pl.) | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** (articles omitted in Turkish) | | **beate** | adjective “blessed” | **kutsal** | “blessed / holy” | OK | | **genti** | noun “folk, people” | **halka** | “people / crowd” | OK |

### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: *che* (both occurrences), *son*, *a*, *le* – Turkish does not need these grammatical particles/articles; their meaning is conveyed implicitly. - No **MISSING**, **WRONG**, or **GRAMMAR** issues were detected in the Turkish rendering.
